help_exact:
Pair this device with another (short-code + fingerprint exchange)

Usage: entangle pair [OPTIONS] [CODE]

Arguments:
  [CODE]
          The 6-digit code, positionally: `entangle pair 734-291`

Options:
      --allow-local
          Use local in-process kernel (no daemon, no persistent state). For testing only.
          
          When the daemon is not running, commands normally fail with an actionable error. Pass this flag (or set ENTANGLE_ALLOW_LOCAL=1) to fall back to a short-lived in-process kernel instead.  State is NOT shared with any running daemon.

      --responder
          Act as the responder: show a pairing code and wait for the other device

      --display-name <DISPLAY_NAME>
          Human-readable display name for this device (default: hostname)

      --manual
          Use the copy-paste blob channel instead of the network.
          
          For air-gapped machines, or networks where mDNS/QUIC cannot cross. Implied by any of the `--*-file` blob options.

      --peer <PEER>
          (Initiator) Pair with this device instead of browsing: either a `<pubkey-hex>@<host>:<port>` long address, or a peer id / name prefix matching one discovered device

      --code <CODE>
          The 6-digit code shown on the other device (skips the prompt).
          
          Spec §6.3 spells the initiator's invocation `entangle pair 734-291`, so the code is also accepted as a positional argument.

  -y, --yes
          Do not ask for confirmation before storing the peer

      --timeout <SECS>
          (Responder) Seconds to wait for a device before giving up
          
          [default: 300]

      --max-attempts <N>
          (Responder) Wrong codes tolerated before the session is destroyed
          
          [default: 5]

      --discover-secs <SECS>
          (Initiator) Seconds to browse for devices in pairing mode
          
          [default: 4]

      --emit-request-file <PATH>
          (Initiator) Write the REQUEST blob to this file instead of stdout

      --consume-accept-file <PATH>
          (Initiator) Read the ACCEPT blob from this file instead of stdin

      --emit-finalize-file <PATH>
          (Initiator) Write the FINALIZE blob to this file instead of stdout

      --request-file <PATH>
          (Responder) Read the REQUEST blob from this file instead of stdin

      --emit-accept-file <PATH>
          (Responder) Write the ACCEPT blob to this file instead of stdout

      --consume-finalize-file <PATH>
          (Responder) Read the FINALIZE blob from this file instead of stdin

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

Paste this FINALIZE blob to the other device:

✓ added to <disposable-directory>/manual/A/.entangle/peers.toml

scope: Disposable homes/Ed25519 keys on a single Linux host. Manual channel uses PTY transfers. Default network channel uses a direct loopback QUIC address with mDNS disabled to isolate the test.
redactions: Pairing codes, signed exchange blobs, disposable fingerprints, keys, peer IDs, temporary paths and ephemeral port are replaced. Fixed prompt wording is preserved.
